Then, calculate the discriminant (Δ = b² - 4ac). If Δ > 0, there are two real roots. Use the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a) to find the roots. If Δ = 0, there is one real root. To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x to find the critical points. Then, find the second derivative of the function, f''(x). Evaluate the second derivative at each critical point. If f''(x) > 0, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the test is inconclusive.
